disposition_reason: Concentrations of eight metals in five vegetables were measured; this PDF lacks Figure 1 and Tables 3-5, so only the eight extreme values printed in the results text are extracted.

study.design: Market survey with daily intake and hazard quotient
study.market: Building Materials (Express), Farin Gada, Bukuru (Kugia), Terminus and Fobur markets, Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria
study.method: HClO4/HNO3 Kjeldahl digestion of 0.2 g; graphite furnace AAS (PG500)
study.qa: Triplicate readings of each digest; no CRM or recovery reported

findings.group: Composite of purchases from 3 traders in each of 5 Jos markets
findings.integrity_flag: Section 3.2 daily intakes (e.g. arsenic 5.535-11.378 mg/day) are 1000 times what these concentrations give at the stated 61.5 g/day intake, so a concentration or intake unit is mislabeled
findings.notes: Value printed in the results text (highest or lowest of its metal across the vegetables); the full results are in Figure 1, which is not in this PDF. Washed, air-dried two weeks and ground; dry basis inferred. Dispersion assumed SD (not defined).

Section 3.2 daily intakes are 1000x the values implied by the text concentrations at 61.5 g/day.
Collection dates not reported; number of samples per vegetable is one composite per vegetable (5 markets x 3 traders).
